subject: Connector IP protection allocation — scope, cap, and evidence sync
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightdelta.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightdelta.com
Date: Sun, 7 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form — connectors & IP allocation

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Two follow-ups from our side after legal looked through the MSA + order form:

1) We use multiple third-party connectors in our product (some maintained by small vendors). Our counsel is concerned about the breadth of the IP indemnity in section 6: it looks like Redwood would remain responsible for third-party IP claims even when the claim arises from our use of a vendor connector that BrightDelta selected and integrated.

2) Procurement asked us to surface a clearer evidence and notice workflow — they want concrete SLAs for initial notice, evidence preservation, and a named point of contact to expedite mitigation.

BrightDelta is fine with a defense obligation where Redwood’s product causes infringement, but they want carveouts where the issue stems from: (a) third-party connector vendor code that BrightDelta chose/installed, or (b) BrightDelta custom configurations that materially change runtime behavior.

Can we get a proposal that: (i) narrows Redwood’s indemnity for connector-origin claims, (ii) provides a per-claim cap tied to order form value for third-party cases, and (iii) includes an evidence template for triage? Procurement wants to avoid open-ended exposure here.

Attaching BrightDelta’s redlines and a short evidence checklist.

Best,
Laura

Attachments: BrightDelta_redlines_v3.docx (docx), evidence-request-template.pdf (pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightdelta.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connector IP protection allocation — scope, cap, and evidence sync

Laura — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Appreciate procurement surfacing the evidence ask.

Summary of what we can propose from a product + commercial standpoint:
- Limited indemnity carve: Redwood will not assume indemnity for third-party IP claims that arise solely from connector vendor code where: (i) BrightDelta selected and installed the connector, and (ii) Redwood provided only the standard adapter (no custom integration by Redwood). We will propose specific language to trace "solely from connector vendor code."
- Configuration carve: For claims resulting from customer-modified configurations that materially alter request/response handling, Redwood will request that BrightDelta retain responsibility unless Redwood performed the custom work or certified the change.
- Per-claim cap: For third-party connector-origin claims we propose a per-claim cap equal to 150% of the order form annual spend for the connector(s) implicated, with a separate aggregate cap equal to 300% of that spend (subject to standard exceptions for gross negligence/fraud).
- Evidence & notice: We'll adopt a short notice and evidence workflow (48-hour acknowledgement, 5-business-day initial evidence exchange list). We'll provide the evidence-request-template as a starting point and add an RFC-style contact table (names, escalation matrix).

Kimberly — looping you in to confirm the legal framing and whether the per-claim cap numbers are workable. Ben/Jordan — flagging for pricing and ARR impact (we may need to table a small uplift or insurance credit to preserve economics).

If that approach sounds reasonable I can ask legal to produce redline language (MSA + order form) and a short mutual action plan for signature so procurement can close quickly.

Thanks,
Rishi

--

Rishi/Team — thanks for the clear framing. A few legal notes and suggested edits (summary version — I'll push full MSA + order form redlines later today):

1) "Solely from connector vendor code" — suggested test language: "To the extent a claim arises solely and directly from the unmodified, original code of a third-party connector where Customer selected and deployed such connector, Seller's indemnity shall not apply." This preserves a narrow carveout while leaving indemnity intact for mixed-cause claims.

2) Material configuration carveout — propose to require evidence that the customer made the configuration change and a narrow rebuttable presumption where changes are uncertified. This avoids easy finger-pointing.

3) Caps — the proposed 150% per-claim / 300% aggregate for connector-origin claims is reasonable commercially. Legal recommends tying the cap to the annualized fees paid under the specific order form line items for affected connectors and excluding amounts paid for professional services (so the cap scales with recurring spend).

4) Evidence protocol — will include: (a) initial notice template, (b) list of preservation steps, (c) named technical contacts for triage, and (d) a short escrow/forensics clause if required. We should also add a 30-day cooperation period before invoking insurers/escrow to encourage remediation first.

5) Exceptions — carveouts should not apply where Redwood's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of representations causes the claim. Also preserve indemnity for claims stemming from Redwood-supplied components.

Next steps:
- I'll upload a tracked redline for the MSA + order form (edits to indemnity and evidence sections).
- Rishi/Ben: confirm if we want to offer a 3% price uplift on connector lines or a one-time "connector protection fee" in lieu of increasing the cap. Ben, can you run quick margin impact?

Kim

--

Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Kim/Rishi — this is very helpful, thanks. Procurement reviewed the cap language idea and the evidence workflow; procurement is comfortable moving forward if we get: (1) the narrow connector carveout language you proposed, (2) the per-connector annualized-fee cap approach (150%/300% as drafted), and (3) the 48-hour acknowledgement + 5-business-day initial evidence list commitment.

BrightDelta is willing to accept a small one-time connector protection fee in lieu of a permanent price uplift; procurement asked us to propose $8,000 per connector of concern (for up to 3 connectors) to be applied as a one-time order form line item. They'll ask finance to process, but want Redwood to confirm the redline and evidence template so the procurement team can circulate a final PO quickly.
